title: Lift gnocchi out of simmering water with a slotted spoon as they float up, then switch the heat off
instruction: The gnocchi are cooking; each is done when it floats up. Lift them out onto the plate with the slotted spoon as they are done, then put the spoon down and switch the heat off.
context: Restaurant cooks (SOC 35-2014) held about 1.46 million jobs in the United States in 2024 (Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook, Cooks: 1,460,200), and boiling fresh pasta and dumplings to order is regular work at their stations. Fresh gnocchi go into simmering water as a batch, sink, and are done when they float up; they do not surface together. They are soft, so they are lifted out with a slotted spoon as they come up, not poured through a strainer, and one left in the water goes soggy. The cook reads the cue (a piece at the surface), works with a tool in a vessel, keeps the pan where it stands, and ends by switching the heat off. The idea is that of the program's pull request #2048, whose review asked for "a realistic batch of gnocchi" in place of a staged two-at-a-time schedule "while retaining spoon-based retrieval"; scene, kit, numbers and text here are our own.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left. A built-in 30 cm domino induction hob with two zones (sizes of Bosch PIB375FB1E: glass 306 mm wide and 527 mm deep, zones 21.0 and 14.5 cm), lying 6 mm proud of the bench, fixed, its front edge at x 12.75 on the midline; its on/off key (x 14.5, y 7.0) and red lamp (x 14.5, y 4.5) on the front strip. A stainless saute pan, 24 cm across and 7 cm deep inside, with 5.5 cm of cloudy simmering water (4.0 kg with the water), standing loose on the front zone at x 30.5, y 0, its handle pointing away from the arms. Twelve fresh potato gnocchi (26 x 18 x 15 mm, 6 g each, 72 g) on the pan's floor, on the side of the pan away from the right arm, at places drawn from the seed. A 20 cm plate at x 32.5, y -26. A nylon slotted spoon with a cranked handle (334.5 mm, 60 g, bowl 90 x 69 mm and 15 mm deep) with its bowl on a spoon rest at x 71, y -37, handle towards the arms. By seed: when each piece floats up (between 15 and 50 s after the start, each on its own), where each lies and how it is turned.
scoring: A piece counts when it floated, left the water after that and no more than 60 s later, lies on the plate at rest, and was never touched by a gripper (a grasp point within 20 mm of its middle). 0 for the trial if the pan was pushed more than 3 cm from where it stood, or a piece that never floated lies on the plate (raw food served). 0.25: 3 pieces count. 0.5: 6. 0.75: 9, with the heat off and the spoon put down. 1.0: 11 of the 12, with the heat off and the spoon put down. While the heat is on or the spoon is in a gripper the score is never above 0.5. Several pieces to a spoonful are allowed. Real bench: an overhead video gives when each piece comes up and when it leaves the water; the final photo gives the plate, the spoon, the lamp and the pan against the zone's ring. Tipping the pan is not scored: the arms cannot tip a 4 kg pan (shown by a run); its tilt is reported.
reset_notes: A fresh batch of twelve each trial, slid in off a board on the far side of the pan as the trial starts; water topped up to 5.5 cm and back at a simmer; pan centred on the front zone's ring; plate wiped; spoon on its rest with the handle towards the arms; heat on. Gripper pads sleeved against steam and splashes; nothing but the spoon goes into the water.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX. The water is not a fluid: each piece gets lift from the part of it that is under the surface, drag and a slow drift; a raw piece gets 0.78 of the weight of the water it displaces and lies on the floor, a done one 0.916 and floats with 1 mm showing. The water does not act on the spoon, nothing drains or splashes, nothing is hot, and the slots are drawn. The surface is drawn opaque, so a piece on the floor cannot be seen at all. The pieces are rigid boxes; that a gripper may not touch one stands in for squashing it. Stated limits: the spoon as held cannot work the part of the pan nearest the arm that holds it (the pieces are laid on the far side) nor a piece pushed against the far wall (more than about 10 cm from the pan's middle; the top level allows for one piece); in this simulation the spoon does not bring a piece up from the floor, so the raw-food rule can only be met with a hand; the scoop depends on the bowl's height to about 2 mm. Placeholders for measurements on real gnocchi: the times of floating, the draft of a floating piece, drag and drift.
